candidates.change_summary: Delete the require statement, allowing any caller to execute transfers.
Replace `msg.sender == owner` with `true`, removing the ownership check.
Replace `payable(receiver).transfer(amount)` with `payable(owner).transfer(amount)`, sending to owner instead of receiver.
Delete the owner check require statement, allowing anyone to call sendTo.
Replace the owner check with a check that the caller is not the owner.
Replace the transfer call with a transfer of twice the amount.
Replace the transfer call with a transfer of zero amount.
Replace the recipient receiver with the caller msg.sender in the transfer call.
Insert an additional transfer of the amount to the caller before the original transfer.
Delete the require statement enforcing only the owner can call sendTo, allowing any caller to transfer funds.
Change the owner check to require the caller not be the owner, inverting access control.
Removed the owner authorization check and replaced it with a tautological condition, allowing any caller to invoke sendTo.
Reversed the authorization check so only non-owners can successfully call sendTo.
Made the authorization check unconditionally fail by requiring false.
Changed the transfer amount to always be zero.
Changed the transfer recipient to the contract owner instead of the receiver argument.
Changed the transfer to use call instead of transfer, which can forward all available gas and alter failure/reversion behavior.
Replaced transfer with a low-level send whose return value is ignored, changing the failure behavior.
Added an early return before the authorization check so sendTo can complete as a no-op without transferring funds.
Added an early return after the authorization check so sendTo can complete as a no-op for the owner without executing the transfer.
Replace the transfer amount with a fixed zero amount, so no Ether is sent.
Replace the owner check using msg.sender with a comparison against the zero address, allowing unauthorized callers except the zero address.
Delete the require(msg.sender == owner) statement, removing the owner-only restriction.
Replace the require condition msg.sender == owner with msg.sender != owner, inverting the authorization check.
Replace the owner check with a check that the caller is the receiver, changing who is authorized to send.
Replace the transfer amount with 0, making the function send no Ether.
Replace the receiver with msg.sender, causing the function to send Ether back to the caller instead of the intended receiver.
Replace the transfer with a call that ignores the success status, changing failure behavior and gas forwarding.
Remove the ownership check so anyone can call sendTo.
Reverse the ownership check so only non-owners can call sendTo.
Send the transferred amount to the owner instead of the specified receiver.
Send zero instead of the requested amount.
Delete the owner authorization check before transferring funds.
Replace the owner authorization check with an unconditional true require.
Replace the caller authorization check with a check against the receiver.
Send the amount to the caller instead of the requested receiver.
Authorize calls from the receiver instead of the owner.
Replaces the owner check require(msg.sender == owner) with a check that always passes: require(true).
Replaces the owner check require(msg.sender == owner) with a check that always fails: require(false).
Changes the ownership check to compare msg.sender against the receiver instead of owner.
Changes the transfer target from receiver to msg.sender.
Changes the transferred amount from amount to zero.
Deletes the ownership check require(msg.sender == owner), allowing any caller to initiate the transfer.
Deletes the transfer statement so the function performs only the owner check.
